component.name: event
component.title: Event
component.description: Receive the internal events of the CamelContext, such as a route that started or an exchange that failed.
component.label: core,monitoring

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

CamelEventType.label: consumer
CamelEventType.description: The name of the event type, such as RouteStarted or ExchangeCompleted. For a batch, the type of the first event in the List.

CamelEventTimestamp.label: consumer
CamelEventTimestamp.description: The time of the event in milliseconds since the epoch. Only set when the event factory of the CamelContext records timestamps, for example with camel.main.camelEventsTimestampEnabled=true.

CamelEventRouteId.label: consumer
CamelEventRouteId.description: The route ID. For route events, the route that triggered the event. For exchange events, the route the exchange originated from.

CamelEventEndpointUri.label: consumer
CamelEventEndpointUri.description: The endpoint URI. For ExchangeSent/ExchangeSending events, the target endpoint. For other exchange events, the from endpoint of the exchange.

CamelEventException.label: consumer
CamelEventException.description: The exception message from FailureEvent.getCause() (for failure events such as ExchangeFailed, RouteRestartingFailure, ServiceStartupFailure, etc.)

CamelEventDuration.label: consumer
CamelEventDuration.description: The time taken in milliseconds for ExchangeSent events

CamelEventStepId.label: consumer
CamelEventStepId.description: The step ID (for step events such as StepStarted, StepCompleted, StepFailed)

CamelEventRedeliveryAttempt.label: consumer
CamelEventRedeliveryAttempt.description: The redelivery attempt number (for ExchangeRedelivery events)

CamelEventBatchSize.label: consumer
CamelEventBatchSize.description: The number of events in the List body. Only set on a batch, when batchSize is greater than 1.

consumerOut.description: The event, such as a RouteStartedEvent or an ExchangeCompletedEvent. With a batchSize above 1, a List of the events

events.description: A comma-separated list of the event types to consume, as names of the CamelEvent.Type enum, ignoring case, for example RouteStarted,ExchangeFailed. A name that ends with * matches every type that starts with the text before it: Route* matches RouteStarted and also RoutesStarted, and * matches all types. An unknown name fails the creation of the endpoint.

async.description: Whether to put the events in a bounded queue that a pool of threads routes, so the thread that fires an event does not wait for the route. If false, the event is routed on the thread that fires it.

asyncPoolSize.description: The number of threads that take the events from the queue and route them. Only used when async is true.

asyncQueueSize.description: The capacity of the bounded event queue used when async is enabled. When the queue is full, the backpressure policy determines the behavior. Only used when the async option is enabled.

backpressurePolicy.description: What happens to an event when the async queue is full. Block makes the thread that fires the event wait for space, Drop discards the event with a DEBUG log, and Fail throws an exception, which Camel logs at WARN and ignores, so the event is lost.

batchSize.description: The number of events to collect into one exchange, whose body is a java.util.List of the events. A batch is sent when it is full, and every batchTimeout with the events collected so far. With 0 or 1, each event is its own exchange, with the event as the body.

batchTimeout.description: The interval in milliseconds at which a timer sends the events collected so far, even if the batch is not full. Only used when batchSize is greater than 1.

customEventClass.description: The fully qualified name of an event class. The consumer drops an event that is not an instance of this class, in addition to the event types of the path. Use it with the Custom event type to consume only your own events of this class.

exclude.description: A comma-separated list of route IDs. The consumer drops a route event of one of these routes, and an exchange event of an exchange that one of these routes created. It applies after the include option, and does not affect events without a route.

include.description: A comma-separated list of route IDs. The consumer drops a route event of another route, and an exchange event of an exchange that another route created. Events without a route, such as CamelContext and service events, are always consumed.

exceptionHandler.label: consumer,advanced
exceptionHandler.description: To let the consumer use a custom ExceptionHandler. Notice if the option bridgeErrorHandler is enabled then this option is not in use. By default the consumer will deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

exchangePattern.label: consumer,advanced
exchangePattern.description: Sets the exchange pattern when the consumer creates an exchange.
